questions.q: How do the Constitution and laws help confront the marginalisation of Dalits and Adivasis?
answer: The marginalised use the Constitution and special laws to claim equality and dignity.

answer.text: The Constitution abolishes untouchability under Article 17, forbids discrimination on grounds of caste, religion, race, sex or birthplace, and protects the culture and education of minorities under Articles 29 and 30.

The reservation policy sets aside seats in education, government jobs and legislatures for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes. The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act of 1989 protects Dalits and Adivasis from violence and humiliation, and the law against manual scavenging ended that degrading practice.
Communities and social movements use these rights and laws, along with protest, to fight discrimination, though effective implementation remains a challenge.

questions.q: How do Fundamental Rights help communities challenge social injustice and untouchability?

answer.text: give every citizen legal tools to fight discrimination, and marginalised groups have used them to demand justice.

list: The right to equality forbids discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth
Untouchability is abolished and its practice in any form is a punishable offence
Citizens can move the courts directly if their Fundamental Rights are violated

answer.text: special laws like the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act protect Dalits and Adivasis from violence and humiliation, giving communities a means to confront injustice through the law.

questions.q: How do social movements and struggles help marginalised communities claim their rights?

answer.text: do not depend on laws alone; they organise and struggle to make their rights real.

list: They form organisations and movements to demand dignity, land and fair treatment
They use protests, petitions and the courts to press their claims

answer.text: They give the excluded a voice.

list: Movements have won recognition of rights over land and forests and forced the state to act against discrimination
By insisting that the promises of the Constitution be honoured, these struggles push society towards greater equality and justice
